data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A single evaluation distinguishes genuine reliability gain by measuring whether the panel, when asked to justify its answers, provides rationales that cite task-internal features not named in the checklist; if the panel cites only checklist items, it is mere compliance, but if it cites additional structural features that are causally relevant, it has internalized domain structure beyond the checklist.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the panel has internalized the structure but lacks the vocabulary to articulate it, the rationale test will falsely signal mere compliance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert also cites only checklist-like features (because the expert's intuition is opaque even to themselves), the test fails to separate panel from expert on the rationale dimension.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"This is a process-tracing diagnostic. A genuine reliability gain implies the checklist helped the panel access the underlying structure, so the panel's justifications should reference that structure. Mere compliance implies the panel treats the checklist as the only legitimate reasoning pathway, so justifications will be confined to checklist items. The evaluation codes the panel's free-text rationales for checklist-bound vs. checklist-external feature citations.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
